summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain, fever, and cloudy urine, two weeks after a prior hospitalization for pyelonephritis. He has a history of neurogenic bladder with a urostomy and a left nephrostomy tube due to ureteral stricture and severe hydronephrosis. He was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis caused by Escherichia coli, with acute kidney injury on stage IV CKD and hyponatremia. He was started on empiric IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line. His infection resolved, renal function improved, and electrolytes stabilized. He was discharged home with home health services to complete a three-week course of IV antibiotics, with follow-up planned in urology, nephrology, and primary care, including nephrostomy tube management and monitoring of a lung nodule.
